## Natural history notes

A bracket fungus characterized by thin, leathery, fan-shaped to semicircular caps with brown to tan upper surfaces that are often covered in coarse hairs or bristles. In Florida, it is found on dead hardwood branches, logs, stumps, and other decaying wood in hammocks, swamps, forests, parks, and other humid wooded habitats. It acts as a wood-decay fungus, helping break down dead plant material, and its underside has angular to honeycomb-like pores where spores are produced.
